title: Reduction of the pulled-back condensed ell-adic integers
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime, let $X$ be any scheme, and let $r\ge1$, with $\mathbf Z_\ell$ as in [def-weil-l-adic-numbers]. On the small pro-etale site of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $R_X=p_X^*\underline{\mathbf Z}_\ell$ using the coefficient pullback [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point], where $\underline{\mathbf Z}_\ell(S)=C(S,\mathbf Z_\ell)$ is the continuous-function condensed ring [def-sfb-padic-int-condensed-ring], and put $A_{r,X}=(\mathbf Z/\ell^r\mathbf Z)_X$ for the constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let $\rho_r\colon R_X\to A_{r,X}$ be the reduction map: the composite of the canonical ring isomorphism $R_X\cong\varprojlim_{n\geq1}A_{n,X}$ of [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x] in the case $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ (the limit taken along the reduction maps $A_{n+1,X}\to A_{n,X}$) with the projection to the index $r$. Then $\rho_r$ induces an isomorphism of sheaves of rings and $R_X$-modules $$R_X/\ell^rR_X\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{r,X}.$$ Here $\ell^rR_X$ is the image ideal sheaf of multiplication by $\ell^r$, and the quotient is the sheaf quotient, with quotient-ring operations as in [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. These isomorphisms are compatible with the reduction maps for all $r$: $\rho_r$ is $\rho_{r+1}$ followed by $A_{r+1,X}\to A_{r,X}$, so the quotient map $R_X/\ell^{r+1}R_X\to R_X/\ell^rR_X$ corresponds to the reduction $A_{r+1,X}\to A_{r,X}$.

source.place: Integral limit and coefficient extension; the quotient comparison needed to identify the exact upstream Tate construction

proof.text: Apply [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x] with $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$: its final assertion identifies $R_X$ with $\varprojlim_{n\ge1}A_{n,X}$ as sheaves of rings. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise], this limit has sections the compatible tuples $(a_n)_{n\ge1}$; the indexing category is the small ordered set of positive integers with arrows towards smaller indices. The coordinatewise ring operations satisfy the limit universal property, so $\rho_r$ evaluates the $r$-th coordinate and is a ring homomorphism.

source.place: Final paragraph, integral comparison for E = Q_ell; Stacks Tag 00W2 for sectionwise limits

proof.text: For $n,r\ge1$, the additive map $j_{n,r}:\mathbf Z/\ell^n\to\mathbf Z/\ell^{n+r}$, $[k]\mapsto[\ell^rk]$, is injective with image the kernel of reduction to $\mathbf Z/\ell^r$: both claims follow by cancelling $\ell^r$ in the divisibility relation $\ell^{n+r}\mid\ell^rk$. This gives the same assertion on the constant sheaves of [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Indeed, [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] represents sections locally by labels, and equality of their images becomes equality of labels after a further cover. Injectivity on labels therefore gives injectivity on sections. A section in the reduction kernel has, after refining, a label divisible by $\ell^r$; divide that label using $j_{n,r}$. These local divided sections agree on overlaps by injectivity, and hence glue uniquely. Thus every kernel section has a unique divided section in $A_{n,X}$.

source.place: Example constant-sheaf (Tag 0H7J) and Lemma sections-sheafification (Tag 00WK); explicit finite-label divisibility

proof.text: Let $a=(a_n)_n\in R_X(U)$ with $a_r=0$. For each $n\ge1$, $a_{n+r}$ reduces to zero at level $r$, so Step 2 gives a unique $b_n\in A_{n,X}(U)$ with $j_{n,r}(b_n)=a_{n+r}$. Reducing the equation for $b_{n+1}$ to level $n+r$ gives $j_{n,r}(b_{n+1}\bmod\ell^n)=a_{n+r}$; uniqueness gives $b_{n+1}\bmod\ell^n=b_n$. The sectionwise limit of [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise] yields $b\in R_X(U)$. Reducing $j_{n,r}(b_n)=a_{n+r}$ to level $n$ gives $\ell^rb_n=a_n$, hence $\ell^rb=a$. Conversely $(\ell^rb)_r=0$. Consequently $\ker\rho_r(U)=\ell^rR_X(U)$ for every $U$; this presheaf image is already the kernel sheaf, so it also equals the image ideal sheaf in the statement.

source.place: Integral inverse-limit comparison; explicit compatible-coordinate kernel calculation

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local], any section of $A_{r,X}$ is locally the image of a label $c\in\mathbf Z/\ell^r$. Choose an integer representative $k$ of $c$. On each covering object the labels $[k]\in\mathbf Z/\ell^n$ define compatible sections of $A_{n,X}$ for all $n$, hence a section of $R_X$ by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise] and Step 1. Its $r$-th coordinate is $c$. This proves local surjectivity of $\rho_r$; no assertion that these lifts themselves glue is needed.

source.place: Tags 0H7J and 00WK, constant sheaves and local representatives; Tag 00W2 for the compatible tuple

proof.text: Form the presheaf of quotient rings $P(U)=R_X(U)/\ell^rR_X(U)$, with operations and quotient maps of [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Step 3 makes its map $\varphi:P\to A_{r,X}$ injective on every object; Step 4 makes it locally surjective. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-iso-locally-bijective], applied to the underlying additive presheaves, makes $\varphi^\#:P^\#\to A_{r,X}$ an isomorphism. This $P^\#$ is the sheaf quotient: a morphism from $R_X$ to a sheaf annihilating $\ell^rR_X$ factors uniquely through each quotient $P(U)$, compatibly with restrictions, and then uniquely through sheafification by [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. The same argument for ring maps gives its quotient ring operations. The induced map preserves these operations since it is induced locally by the ring maps $\rho_r$; its inverse preserves them by bijectivity. We have the required ring isomorphism.

source.place: Sheafification universal property (Tag 00WH); local bijectivity criterion as stated in the cited node

proof.text: Give $A_{r,X}$ its $R_X$-action through $\rho_r$. For local representatives $a,x\in R_X$, the quotient map satisfies $\overline{ax}\mapsto\rho_r(a)\rho_r(x)$, so the ring isomorphism of Step 5 is $R_X$-linear. Finally the projections in [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x] satisfy $\rho_r=\operatorname{red}_{r+1,r}\rho_{r+1}$. Since $\ell^{r+1}R_X\subseteq\ell^rR_X$, the quotient transition is induced by the identity of $R_X$. Both composites send the class of every local $x$ to $\rho_r(x)$; local representatives in the sheaf quotients therefore give equality of the two morphisms. This proves the claimed compatibility for all $r$.

lean.statement: theorem pur_condensed_zl_reduction_mod_ell_power (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (X : Scheme.{u}) : ∃ (m : ∀ n : ℕ, MonObj (purZlQuotient ℓ X (n + 1)).X) (e : ∀ n : ℕ, purZlQuotient ℓ X (n + 1) ≅ purZlResidueModule ℓ X (n + 1)), (∀ n : ℕ, @IsMonHom _ _ _ _ _ (coefficientRing X (Mon.mk (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj ℤ_[ℓ]))).mon (m n) (purZlQuotientProjection ℓ X (n + 1)).hom ∧ @IsMonHom _ _ _ _ _ (m n) ((sfbConstantRing X).obj ((sfbZModCoefficientTower ℓ).obj (op (n + 1)))).mon (e n).hom.hom ∧ @IsMonHom _ _ _ _ _ ((sfbConstantRing X).obj ((sfbZModCoefficientTower ℓ).obj (op (n + 1)))).mon (m n) (e n).inv.hom ∧ (purZlQuotientProjection ℓ X (n + 1)).hom ≫ (e n).hom.hom = (purZlReduction ℓ X (n + 1)).hom) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, purZlReduction ℓ X (n + 2) ≫ (sfbZModCoefficientTower ℓ ⋙ sfbConstantRing X).map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ (n + 1))).op = purZlReduction ℓ X (n + 1)) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, ∃ t : purZlQuotient ℓ X (n + 2) ⟶ purZlQuotient ℓ X (n + 1), purZlQuotientProjection ℓ X (n + 2) ≫ t = purZlQuotientProjection ℓ X (n + 1) ∧ t.hom ≫ (e n).hom.hom = (e (n + 1)).hom.hom ≫ ((sfbZModCoefficientTower ℓ ⋙ sfbConstantRing X).map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ (n + 1))).op).hom)
lean.note: The canonical reduction is the normalized completed-coefficient limit projection, transported through its cyclic constant-ring comparisons. The sheaf quotient is Mod.cokernelObj of scalar multiplication. The single theorem supplies its quotient ring operations and a module isomorphism preserving ring operations in both directions, with the quotient projection equation and all positive-exponent transition squares. Helper definitions expose precisely these constructions; no dependency or natural-language statement is changed.
